summary: Phase 13 QA audit. I ran these regression suites one file at a time, and all of them passed: phase13_wishlist_alerts 2/2, phase12_marketing 9/9, phase07_payments 7/7 and phase10_admin 4/4. They cover webhook dedupe, the rule that a redirect never marks an order paid, partial refunds with the commission and ledger, role permissions and coupon funding. I added two new suites. test_phase13_qa_audit.py passed 9 of 10: the CSRF origin guard, Mongo operator injection, customer and vendor isolation, upload limits and private files, the login lockout, cron secrets, the granular admin roles and the security-header probe all passed. The 10th test failed: two shoppers were both charged for the last unit. test_phase13_seo_perf.py passed 3/3: the sitemap has 51 URLs and all of them resolve, robots.txt works, and the public endpoints answer in about 0.15-0.2 s. UI checks at 390px on home, shop, product, cart, checkout, account, notifications, wishlist, the vendor dashboard, admin home and admin marketing found no horizontal overflow, no broken images, no images missing alt text and no JS errors. The customer wishlist toggles (wishlist-alert-price/stock) save and stay set after a reload. The admin wishlist switch and threshold (mk-flag-wishlist, mk-wishlist-threshold) save correctly. I found 2 High issues: overselling of the last unit, and rate limits keyed on the load balancer's IP so every visitor shares the same limits. I also found 4 Medium and 9 Low issues.

critical.issue: HIGH - Overselling. Stock is only checked, not reserved, when the Stripe session is created; the reservation happens later in the webhook. Repro: a product with stock 1; two buyers each create a draft and a session (both get 200); both pay. Both orders end up 'paid', inventory is on_hand=1 reserved=1, and the second vendor_order only gets stock_issue=True. Nothing in the API, admin reconciliation, vendor UI or customer UI reads stock_issue, so the second customer is charged for an item that does not exist.

critical.endpoint: core/security.py client_ip (L71-74): all IP-keyed rate limits
critical.issue: HIGH - The rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry is the Google load balancer's IP (34.160.159.238), not the client's (my test traffic left from 34.170.12.145). The rate_limits keys register:/forgot:/analytics: all show 34.160.159.238, both for test traffic and for the Playwright browser. So the whole marketplace shares one bucket: register 10/h, forgot 10/h, contact 5/h, cart 120/min, coupon 20/10min, analytics 300/10min, verify, unsub and invite-accept. Normal traffic can produce 429s for everyone. The login 'IP+email' key also becomes per-email, so anyone can lock any account for 15 min with 5 bad passwords.

minor.issue: MEDIUM - Only nosniff is sent. Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options (or CSP frame-ancestors) and Referrer-Policy are missing on both the API and the SPA, so the admin console can be framed (clickjacking).
MEDIUM (privacy) - Outside production nothing restricts who receives email. Wishlist digests, marketing and receipts would go to any real address stored in the preview DB.

MEDIUM - The 9:00 ET schedule depends on the cron platform honouring 'timezone: America/New_York'. send_hour_et is stored in the flags but the code never reads it. If the timezone key is ignored, digests go out at 09:00 UTC (4-5 AM ET).

MEDIUM (consumer-protection/legal) - The reference price moves up to any higher current price. A vendor can raise the price for one daily run and then return to the old price, and shoppers get an 'X% off' alert based on an inflated price that was only live briefly.

LOW - Alert records are inserted before the daily digest slot is claimed. A change detected after that day's digest went out (or past max_items) is marked as alerted but never emailed, and it won't be resent the next day.

LOW - File contents are never checked against the declared type. HTML bytes uploaded as image/png for a logo are accepted (201). This is mitigated because the file is served as image/png with nosniff.
LOW - Requests that change state are allowed when the Origin header is missing. Browsers do send Origin on cross-site POSTs, so the risk is small; checking Referer as a fallback would close it.
LOW - The failure log message is hard-coded as 'low-stock digest failed' for every job. Failed cron_runs also trigger no alert.
LOW - The reported version is stale: '0.9.0-phase09', phase 9.

ui_bugs.issue: The label '(5% or more)' is hard-coded and ignores the admin threshold. setAlert and change have no .catch, so a failure shows no error toast, and setAlert shows no success toast either.
The input accepts decimals such as 0.5. Saving then shows the raw backend message 'Input should be greater than or equal to 100', which is in basis points rather than percent.

issues: No canonical, OG tags or JSON-LD. Only the product page has them (product canonical, OG and 1 JSON-LD block are present).
On mobile the cookie banner covers about 30% of the viewport until the visitor chooses (expected, noted).
Radix switches pref-*-email/in_app and the filter-in-stock / filter-vendor-* buttons have no text or aria-label for screen readers. Add an aria-label.

34 lines. Missing: a backup restore procedure (mongodump/mongorestore steps, RPO/RTO, restore drill), monitoring and alerting (health probe, 5xx rate, cron_runs failures, email failures), and log retention.

action_items: HIGH: Hold stock when the Stripe Checkout session is created. Use reserve() with the $expr guard in api/v1/payments.py around L55-60, store the reservation on the payment, and release it on cancel, checkout.session.expired and payment failure. In mark_paid, if reserve fails: set the payment to needs_review, add an issue to /admin/payments/reconciliation, notify admin, vendor and customer, and refund the affected lines. test_phase13_qa_audit::test_10 must pass afterwards.

HIGH: Fix client_ip to use a trusted hop count, e.g. TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS in the env, then fwd.split(',')[-(hops+1)]. First log the raw X-Forwarded-For once in preview and production to confirm the hop count, and never trust the leftmost entry blindly.

MEDIUM: Add Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors 'none') and Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin in the core/logging.py middleware, and the same headers at the frontend host or ingress.
MEDIUM: In core/email.py, when APP_ENV != production, send only to an allowlist (example.com, resend.dev, ADMIN_EMAIL, or an EMAIL_TEST_ALLOWLIST env) and log-skip everything else.
MEDIUM: Make the 9:00 ET send time enforced by code: run the wishlist cron hourly and skip unless now.astimezone(ET).hour == cfg['send_hour_et'].
MEDIUM: Don't let a briefly raised price become the reference. Raise ref_price_minor only after the higher price has held N days (store ref_set_at), or use the 30-day low.

LOW: Fix the wishlist alert ordering (claim the digest first, or carry undelivered alerts into the next digest); check upload magic bytes; set a correct cron failure log message and alert on failures; update the health version; add Seo to home and shop; make the UI threshold label dynamic and add error toasts; add aria-labels to icon switches; extend the runbook with restore and monitoring.
critical_code_review_comments: vendor_orders.stock_issue is written but never read anywhere in the backend or frontend.
run_wishlist_alerts makes N+1 queries per shopper, serially (users.find_one plus a products query each). That's fine now, but batch it when wishlists grow.

Good: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere. JSON-LD is injected via script.text and the backend escapes '</'. Email templates escape user values. Review photos are served only when approved and the review is public. Verification docs are private. cta_url patterns block '//host' and javascript: URLs. Cron and webhook use hmac.compare_digest plus a run-id dedupe.

Good: auth cookies are httpOnly, Secure and SameSite=None. The foreign-Origin guard returns 403 with a request_id. Error responses include request_id. No secrets or PII found in the last 3000 backend log lines.

success_rate.backend: 96% (35/36 tests across 6 files; the only failure is the oversell finding)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of the flows checked (mobile layouts, wishlist toggles, admin switch)

seed_data_creation: None kept. I created TEST6_/TEST_ users, vendors, products, orders, payments, tickets, files and role admins, then deleted them through the module teardowns and by id. I also removed 3 leftover TEST_Vendor users, 24 orphan notifications and 358 audit logs written by test or super-admin actors during the window. 44 system audit entries (actor None, e.g. payment.succeeded) remain. platform_settings marketing.flags was absent before testing; I deleted the doc my UI save created, so it is absent again (defaults apply). Stripe test-mode PaymentIntents remain in Stripe test mode.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the suites one file at a time: pytest tests/test_phase13_qa_audit.py, tests/test_phase13_seo_perf.py, tests/test_phase13_wishlist_alerts.py. For UI, `python -m tests.qa13_ui_sessions` (from /app/backend) writes customer, vendor and admin cookies to /tmp/qa13_sessions.json and creates a 'TEST QA13 Kente Scarf' product; inject the cookies in Playwright, then run `python -m tests.qa13_ui_sessions cleanup`. After the main agent's fixes, recheck test_10 (oversell) and the rate_limits key IP (it should be the client IP, not 34.160.159.238).
rca of the issue: Oversell: the availability check in payments.py (_validate before the Stripe session) is not atomic and holds nothing, and reserve() only runs in mark_paid after the money is captured. A failed reserve() just sets stock_issue. Rate-limit IP: behind Cloudflare and the Google LB, the last proxy appends its own address as the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry, so client_ip always returns the LB IP.
